gap: No result ChatGPT got states that Notebookcheck measured the Amazfit Active 2 reading low against a Polar H10 chest strap (3.77% average deviation, up to 5 bpm, consistently under) and lasting only 3–4 days with all tracking and the always-on display enabled, against Amazfit's 10-day claim.
standout_why: Pages I could read: our own dealectric.com page has no independent measurements; its battery and GPS figures are maker claims. roxskin.io (cited in the third chat) has no measurements for any candidate. It says the site did not lab-test anything, and its only race-mode figures cover the Amazfit Balance 3. I could not read three rivals' bodies: tomsguide.com/best-picks/best-running-watches and techradar.com/best/cheap-running-watch (both cited) came back with only their titles, and roxgrit.com and wearablebeat.com failed to load (bad certificate, 403). ChatGPT's own answers quote only claimed battery figures ('up to 10 days', '14 days') and give no measured heart-rate or battery figure. The Notebookcheck Active 2 figures and the OutdoorGearLab PACE 3 and Forerunner 55 chest-strap figures are new as far as I could check. One limit: Tom's Guide and TechRadar may cite reviewer measurements I could not see.
decides: This confirms the Active 2 pick and doesn't overturn it, because the HYROX race mode is still the deciding feature and no reviewer has measured the Bip 6. It does put numbers behind ChatGPT's advice to add a chest strap. Notebookcheck found the Active 2 under-reads heart rate against a Polar H10. OutdoorGearLab measured the PACE 3 within ±1.54 bpm and the Forerunner 55 within ±1.68 bpm of a Polar H10 on a 0.5-mile run. The methods differ (bike against run, percent against bpm), so the numbers can't be ranked head to head. Battery should be presented as about 3–4 days with everything on, not '10 days'.
